Alice — thanks for the matrix and the clear list. Looping in Karthik (network/runtime), Ben (onboarding ops) and Kimberly (security/compliance).

Quick summary of what we can provide now and what we need from you to map to Redwood gates: 

What Redwood will provide (short):
- KMS integrations: we support cloud KMS (customer-managed key) for private control plane and HSM-backed KMS for air-gapped installs. We'll include our KMS certificate exchange process in the evidence pack.
- Egress model: recommended pattern is dual-path routing — primary VPC peering / private link to Dedicated control plane; fallback via regionally scoped egress with strict allowlist. We'll document the routing behavior and SLO impact.
- Observability: required endpoints = /health, /metrics (Prometheus format), and an optional traces endpoint (OTLP). We allow customer-run collectors behind an internal endpoint; outbound telemetry is optional and configurable.
- Portability artifacts: model binary, compilation profile, kernel selection manifest, and model-variant metadata. We will provide a migration checklist for any quantized variants.

Action items I propose (owners + rough dates):
1) Karthik: produce a "networking + port" concise checklist against your matrix — EOD Tue 27 Jul (attachment: redwood-portability-guidelines-v1.pdf).
2) Ben: assemble a compliance evidence packet (SLA excerpt, architecture diagram, data flows) — Wed 28 Jul.
3) Kimberly: review MediCorp matrix against SOC2 / customer-hosted controls and flag gaps — Thu 29 Jul.

Can you confirm a good time window for a 30 min tech-run on Thu 29 Jul? Also — which environment will be used for the smoke test (staging or customer-provided preprod)?

Thanks — putting a short preflight mapping in the shared Drive folder and will follow up with the first draft.

— Soojin Lee

Alice / team — I reviewed the MediCorp matrix and sketched a compact technical checklist below. I'm keeping it focused on the gating items we'll validate during the network smoke test.

Network & hosting checklist (high priority) — to be validated by MediCorp and Redwood during smoke test:
- IP ranges: provide CIDR blocks for control-plane peering and for workload egress; ensure no overlap with Redwood reserved prefixes.
- NAT/Bastion: recommend a dedicated NAT instance or managed NAT gateway for outbound token refresh calls; a bastion host with MFA + jumpbox for initial access.
- DNS: internal DNS records for control-plane endpoints; CNAMEs for certificate issuance.
- Firewall ports (minimum):
  - 443 TCP outbound to control-plane (control API)
  - 853/4317/4318 (OTLP/traces) optional outbound to telemetry collectors
  - 5222 TCP if using a persistent control websocket (depends on runtime variant)
  - 22 TCP for admin bastion (restrict to jumpbox IPs)
  - NTP (UDP 123) for clock sync
- MTU: set to 9001 if using jumbo frames between nodes; ensure LB / firewall preserves MTU.
- TLS & certs: provide CSR for mutual TLS where mTLS is requested; list of CA roots we'll accept.
- KMS / key exchange: exchange public KMS service endpoints, required IAM roles, and sample value rotation schedule.
- Observability: expose /metrics on :9102 and an internal OTLP collector endpoint if using tracing.
- Quotas & resource limits: relay expected RPS and token/s throughput so we can size GPU pools and networking NAT throughput.

Low/medium priority (nice-to-have for cutover):
- BGP peering or route reflector if you plan cross-region on-prem clusters
- IP allowlist for image registry pull endpoints
- Dedicated SNAT pool to avoid ephemeral port exhaustion at scale

I attached a short CSV (networking-ports-reference.csv) with port numbers and direction to map against your matrix. If MediCorp can return the matrix with columns for "owner" and "test-verified" I can mark items off during the smoke test.

I'll be online 10–12 PDT Wed if you want a quick walkthrough.

— Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: networking-ports-reference.csv (csv)
